newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JUNE 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JUNE 4.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou asserted yesterday that there would be no change in Greek economic policy despite the optimism created by the win by French leftists of a 'more human' Maastricht.
--Plans to implement alternatives to military service for conscientious objectors have caused friction in ruling party PASOK and objections from opposition party MPs.
--The government is concerned by the wave of euphoria sweeping Europe in the wake of the French election results and is stressing there will be no let-up in austerity, at least this year.
--Plans have been drawn up for the voluntary retirement of 3,000 workers at 14 ailing state-run firms. The cost of the plan is budgeted at 20 billion drachmas.
--A prosecutor will face his colleagues at a disciplinary hearing after "forgetting" a file of charge sheets which led to their being written off.
--The tax department is now processing all those with debts to the state, in the hope of collecting one trillion drachmas in outstanding payments.
--Forthcoming municipal elections are considered to be a test of the strength of the centre-left's standing in Greece, and a barometer of the popularity of ruling party PASOK.
--The Supreme Court yesterday ruled that both parents were entitled to receive family benefits paid to public servants, paving the way for a flurry of suits claiming retroactive payment.
--Opposition to plans to merge communities and villages - part of the interior ministry's reforms aimed at restructuring local government - is slowly building throughout the country.
--Former public order minister Stelios Papathemelis has been called to testify regarding recent statements that his ministry knew of November 17 terrorists but did nothing.
